newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen futures dip with weaker U.S. bonds.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen futures dip with weaker U.S. bonds.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures were easier but off their lows in late Friday trade following steep overnight losses in U.S. treasuries.
Dealers said U.S. bonds were again hit by strong economic data on Thursday, fuelling fears of an interest rate hike in the first quarter after a fierce sell-off on December 31.
An unexpected rise in the National Association of Purchasing Management Index to 54.0 in December from 52.7 in November was the main factor depressing sentiment on Thursday, dealers said.
September Euroyen was quoted at 99.19 at 1120 GMT, unchanged against its IMM close after hitting a low of 99.15. June was at 99.33 against 99.34.

A Japanese bank dealer said concerns about a U.S. rate hike would weigh on Japanese government bond (JGB) futures when Tokyo players return from holiday on Monday, as the Bank of Japan is generally expected to follow the Federal Reserve in raising rates.
"99.22/23 will be a crucial level," he said, adding that September Euroyen could hit resistance there before backing off.

But a trader with a U.S. institution said JGB and Euroyen futures were unlikely to see further declines. "They're hitting support levels right now so there could be a quick buy-up on Monday," he said.
JGB futures were not traded due to the holiday in Japan.
Eurodollar futures ended firmer after opening sharply lower following overnight declines in Chicago.

Dealers said they were likely to trade sideways with a downside bias until next week. But a smattering of second-tier U.S. economic data, including November construction spending, could provide an excuse to sell if the numbers exceed forecasts.
"June Eurodollars should go back above 94.23 tonight but I have questions about whether they can hold above there," said the Japanese bank dealer.
March Eurodollars ended at 94.40 against their IMM close at 94.38. June were at 94.21 against 94.19.
